questions.q: What's the difference between an inline dataset and a dataset object as a source?
options: A dataset object is reusable across flows and activities; an inline dataset is defined directly in the source, ideal for flexible or parameterized sources
Inline datasets can never be used in a mapping data flow
Dataset objects only work with SQL sources
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: Dataset objects suit a hardened, stable, reusable schema. Inline datasets live natively in Spark and suit flexible schemas, one-off sources, or heavy parameterization.

questions.q: What does Allow schema drift do on a source?
options: Lets new source columns not in the defined schema flow through the data flow anyway
Deletes any column not already defined in the schema
Forces the data flow to fail if any column is missing
Only applies to SQL Server sources
questions.explain: Schema drift lets flexible, changing source schemas pass through without needing to explicitly redefine columns every time.

options: Fails the data flow outright if the incoming data doesn't match the defined schema exactly
Automatically fixes mismatched column types
Only validates the sink, never the source
Skips schema checking entirely for faster runs
questions.explain: Validate schema is a strict check — any mismatch between the incoming data and the defined projection causes the run to fail.

questions.q: What does the Projection tab define?
options: The source's columns, types, and formats
Which integration runtime executes the data flow
The pipeline's trigger schedule
The sink's file naming pattern only
questions.explain: Projection defines the shape of the source data — its columns, data types, and formats — either imported live or manually detected.

options: Where a data flow's transformed data actually gets written — the mirror image of a source
A type of trigger for scheduling pipelines
A control activity for branching pipeline logic
Another name for the Copy activity
questions.explain: Every data flow needs at least one sink — where the transformed data lands, configured similarly to a source, including its own Allow schema drift option.
